parsed.notes: Lens A found one support-tightening issue: the holding should preserve the opinion's burden/no-evidence wording about May-Shaw's right to exclude others.

reasons: The lake identity record identifies the case as United States v. Christopher May-Shaw, decided by the Sixth Circuit on 2020-04-08.
The lake citation display is 955 F.3d 563, with year 2020 and court 6th Cir. 2020.

defect.evidence_quote: there is no evidence that May-Shaw had any legal right to exclude others from the carport.
defect.problem: The holding is substantially supported, but it overstates the exclusion-right predicate by saying May-Shaw 'had no right to exclude others.' The opinion says there was no evidence that he had such a legal right, which matters because the court framed the issue through May-Shaw's burden.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: 'where May-Shaw regularly parked but produced no evidence that he had a legal right to exclude others, and which was easily viewable from a public street...' Consider also phrasing the curtilage point as 'failed to establish curtilage.'

reasons: The opinion affirms denial of suppression.
The opinion states the carport was in a communal parking lot, close to the apartment, and easily viewable from Norman Drive.
The opinion states: 'May-Shaw has failed to establish that the carport constituted the curtilage of his apartment; the drug dog sniff therefore did not constitute a search.'
The opinion also holds the twenty-three-day pole-camera surveillance did not violate May-Shaw's reasonable expectation of privacy.
residual_risks: The proposition should retain the burden-of-proof nuance to avoid converting an evidentiary failure into an affirmative property-right finding.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'no evidence of a legal right to exclude others' and 'failed to establish curtilage' rather than absolute formulations.

reasons: Curtilage is the central issue in the opinion's dog-sniff analysis.
The opinion applies the Dunn factors to decide whether the carport was curtilage and concludes May-Shaw failed to establish it was.
Treatment and currency are outside lens A; no treatment defect is raised.
The disclosed lake identity confirms a Sixth Circuit court-of-appeals decision, and the content label is internally consistent with that disclosed identity.
residual_risks: Treatment-weight review is reserved to lens B.
